group: two periodic regions converting into each other
title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC0LF_1RD0LB_0RA1RE_1RD---_0RC0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC0LF_1RD0LB_0RA1RE_1RD---_0RC0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape consists of two periodic regions with a few dozen defects; the head converts one region into the other a word at a time (proved in Lean), and the sizes of the regions go up and down as the tape grows. The machine can only stop when the head in state D reads two 1s, which the sweeps never do. The C simulator runs 1011 steps without a halt; the dynamics of the defects has not been worked out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,247 cells have been visited and 30,462 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.012). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494).

claims.title: The sweeps
claims.text: In state E moving right, (00100101)n becomes (10101111)n; in state D, (10100100)n becomes (11110101)n; 8n steps each, for every n and any tape around.

claims.title: When it halts
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when the head in state D reads a 1 followed by a 1 (D1 = 1RE, then E1 is undefined).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 100,000,000,000 steps from blank tape without a halt.

claims.title: Two regions and a few defects
claims.text: Tapes sampled up to 1.6·10<sup>9</sup> steps consist of the two periodic regions (4,483 to 14,968 single 1s, 3,727 to 5,309 blocks of five) and only 21 to 48 defect blocks.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Whether the motion of the defects is regular (a counter) or chaotic, and whether it can ever put 1 1 under the head in state D, has not been worked out.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape of this machine is two repeating patterns side by side, with a few dozen irregular spots; the head keeps turning one pattern into the other. It has run 10<sup>11</sup> steps without stopping.

facts.text: The only way it can stop, proved in Lean.
No halt in the C simulator.
Irregular blocks in a tape of tens of thousands of cells.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.012). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,247 cells (34 left of the start, 37,017 right), with a density of 1s of 0.645.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Two patterns and a few defects
html: Almost all of the tape is one of two periodic words: 00100101 (single 1s) and 11111010 (blocks of five 1s). At 1.6·109 steps the tape is 62,321 cells long and holds 14,968 single 1s, 4,141 blocks of five and only 48 other blocks (of 3 to 13 ones).

Sweeping right in state E or D, the head turns 00100101 into a rotation of 11111010, one word every 8 steps; Lean proves this for any number of words. The two regions grow and shrink in turn while the whole tape grows like the square root of the step count.

sections.heading: Open
html: The machine stops only when the head, in state D, reads two 1s in a row. The sweeps never do; a halt would have to come from one of the defects or from a turn at an end of the tape. The plain C simulator runs 1011 steps without a halt. How the defects move has not been worked out.

summary: The tape is two periodic regions (00100101 and 11111010) with a few dozen defects; rightward sweeps convert one into the other a word at a time (proved in Lean), the region sizes oscillate, the tape grows like sqrt(steps). Halts only if D reads 1 1. No halt in 10^11 steps.
